widgets.name: error_landscape
widgets.title: Learning is rolling downhill
widgets.hint: Drag the ball · press play · change the step size
widgets.pitch: An error landscape with local and global minima. Gradient descent steps in the downhill direction proportional to the local slope.

widgets.name: error_landscape_2d
widgets.title: 2D error surface: saddle points, momentum, and SGD noise
widgets.hint: Click the map to drop the walkers · press play · compare plain GD, momentum, and noisy SGD
widgets.pitch: Alternative to Figure 1: a two-parameter contour basin where plain gradient descent stalls in a local trap or saddle plateau, while momentum and stochastic mini-batch noise cross into the global basin.

widgets.name: ols_fit
widgets.title: Fit a line by eye, then by least squares
widgets.hint: Drag the two handles · or drag the line itself
widgets.pitch: Residuals drawn as literal squares: ordinary least squares picks the line with the smallest total square area.
widgets.data_doc: {x: number[], y: number[], xlabel?, ylabel?}

widgets.name: ols_robust
widgets.title: Why squaring matters: outliers and OLS (L2) vs robust (L1) regression
widgets.hint: Drag the red outlier point anywhere on the plot · compare the squared-error and absolute-error lines
widgets.pitch: Alternative to Figure 2: dragging a single high-leverage outlier shows how quadratic squares pull the OLS line, whereas absolute-error (L1 / Huber) regression stays anchored to the bulk of the data.
widgets.data_doc: {x: number[], y: number[], xlabel?, ylabel?}

widgets.name: gd_regression
widgets.title: Fitting a line by gradient descent
widgets.hint: Press play · click the error map to pick a new starting line
widgets.pitch: The same line fit, found by walking downhill on the error surface over (slope, intercept).
widgets.data_doc: {x: number[], y: number[], xlabel?, ylabel?}

widgets.name: spline_scaling
widgets.title: Bending the line: piecewise segments and splines
widgets.hint: Press play or scrub K · switch linear vs cubic spline · toggle adaptive knots
widgets.pitch: New addition (from ScalingPessimism resolution scaling): tile a nonlinear curve with K piecewise segments or cubic splines joined at knots. Error falls as a power of K on log-log axes until hitting the noise floor.
widgets.data_doc: {x: number[], y: number[], curve_x?: number[], curve_y?: number[], xlabel?, ylabel?}

widgets.name: spline_relu_basis
widgets.title: Splines as a bank of ReLU hinges (from fixed knots to learned features)
widgets.hint: Drag the orange knot pins along the x-axis · press play to optimize knot locations by gradient descent
widgets.pitch: Alternative to Figure 4: a piecewise-linear spline is a weighted sum of ReLU hinges max(0, x - knot). Dragging or optimizing the knot positions turns fixed-basis spline regression into a 1-layer neural network.
widgets.data_doc: {x: number[], y: number[], xlabel?, ylabel?}

widgets.name: category_manifolds
widgets.title: What categories look like to a machine
widgets.hint: Switch shapes · click to add a point (shift-click for the next category)
widgets.pitch: Categories are clouds (manifolds) in feature space. Some can be split by a straight line; most cannot.
widgets.data_doc: {X: [x, y][], y: int[], names?: string[], xlabel?, ylabel?}

widgets.name: logistic_gd
widgets.title: Logistic regression, learning a boundary
widgets.hint: Press play · scrub through training · change the overlap
widgets.pitch: A probability map sharpens step by step until the boundary matches the closed-form (sklearn) solution.
widgets.data_doc: {X: [x, y][], y: 0|1[], names?: [string, string], xlabel?, ylabel?}

widgets.name: logistic_link
widgets.title: Why not fit a straight line to 0 / 1 labels? The sigmoid link
widgets.hint: Slide the extreme point · drag steepness · watch the threshold at y = 0.5
widgets.pitch: Alternative to Figure 6: fitting a straight OLS line directly to 0/1 outcomes predicts probabilities below 0% and above 100% and gets skewed by easy extreme points; the logistic sigmoid clamps predictions to [0, 1].
widgets.data_doc: {x: number[], y: 0|1[], names?: [string, string], xlabel?}

widgets.name: perceptron
widgets.title: A linear perceptron, live
widgets.hint: Press play or step · click the plane to add points (shift-click for the other class)
widgets.pitch: The classic single-neuron classifier: weighted inputs, a threshold, and an update rule that nudges weights after each mistake.

widgets.name: mlp_xor
widgets.title: Folding the plane: how one hidden layer solves XOR
widgets.hint: Press play to train · watch the hidden hinges fold the four corners into a separable cloud
widgets.pitch: Alternative to Figure 7: where a single perceptron fails on XOR, a hidden layer of ReLU hinges folds the input plane so the opposite corners become linearly separable.

widgets.name: classifier_zoo
widgets.title: One dataset, five classifiers
widgets.hint: Pick a model · slide its main setting · watch train vs test accuracy
widgets.pitch: Real scikit-learn decision surfaces, precomputed in Python across each model's main hyperparameter.
widgets.data_doc: Output of ml4hl.zoo.decision_grids(X, y) (one or more datasets).

widgets.name: percolation
widgets.title: Clusters as connected ink
widgets.hint: Slide the disc size · hover a point · switch to exemplar voting
widgets.pitch: Grow a disc around every point: clusters are whatever touches. Then let points vote for exemplars instead.

widgets.name: percolation_grid
widgets.title: Lattice percolation: connected clusters and the critical threshold
widgets.hint: Press play or slide open-bond probability p · toggle all clusters vs largest component
widgets.pitch: Alternative to Figure 9 (from ScalingPessimism): bond percolation on a 2D lattice across the critical phase transition at p_c = 0.50, where local connections suddenly coalesce into a spanning cluster.

widgets.name: kmeans
widgets.title: K-means, one step at a time
widgets.hint: Press play or step · drag a center (the crosses) to restart from there
widgets.pitch: Assign every point to its nearest centroid, move each centroid to the middle of its points, repeat.

widgets.name: gmm_em
widgets.title: Soft responsibilities and oval clusters: Gaussian Mixture EM vs K-means
widgets.hint: Press play or step EM · compare elliptical Gaussian components with spherical K-means
widgets.pitch: Alternative to Figure 10: Expectation-Maximization (EM) fits full covariance ellipses and soft cluster probabilities, succeeding on elongated and overlapping clouds where K-means' Voronoi cells cut across clusters.

widgets.name: dendrogram
widgets.title: Hierarchical clustering: cut the tree
widgets.hint: Drag the dashed cut line · hover a branch to see its members · switch linkage
widgets.pitch: Merge the two closest groups, again and again. Where you cut the resulting tree decides how many clusters you get.
widgets.data_doc: {X: number[][] (any dims), xy?: [x, y][] (display coordinates), labels?: string[]}

widgets.name: autoencoder
widgets.title: An autoencoder squeezes, then rebuilds
widgets.hint: Press train · change the bottleneck · drag a code bar to imagine
widgets.pitch: A network that learns to copy its input through a narrow bottleneck. Self-supervised compression.
widgets.data_doc: {images: number[][] (N x 64 or N x side*side, values 0-1), side?: 8}

widgets.name: projection
widgets.title: Projections: PCA and random
widgets.hint: Drag the line to rotate it (it snaps to the best one) · switch to random projection
widgets.pitch: PCA finds the direction of maximum spread. Random projections preserve pairwise distances across high dimensions.
widgets.data_doc: {X2: [x, y][] (PCA tab), Xhigh?: number[][], labels?: int[] (random tab)}

widgets.name: pca_reconstruct
widgets.title: PCA scree spectrum and profile reconstruction
widgets.hint: Slide the kept components k · click a bar or cycle examples to see what PCA keeps vs drops
widgets.pitch: Alternative to Figure 13: inspect the full eigenvalue scree plot alongside live reconstruction of individual feature profiles as k grows from 1 to d.
widgets.data_doc: {X: number[][], feature_names?: string[]}

widgets.name: rdm_builder
widgets.title: Building and comparing RDMs
widgets.hint: Hover a cell · switch the distance · shuffle the order · run the shuffle test
widgets.pitch: Features to distances to the upper triangle to a second-order comparison between two systems.
widgets.data_doc: {names: string[], A: number[][], B: number[][], groups?: string[], labelA?, labelB?}

widgets.name: rsa_pipeline
widgets.title: End-to-end RSA pipeline: from feature tables to upper triangles to model comparison
widgets.hint: Hover a pair in the RDM or vector barcode · switch candidate model · change distance metric
widgets.pitch: Alternative to Figure 14: explicit four-stage construction showing how two feature tables of different widths become square RDMs, unfold their upper triangles into pair vectors, and score candidate models via Spearman rho.
widgets.data_doc: {names: string[], A: number[][], B: number[][], groups?: string[], labelA?, labelB?}

widgets.name: overfitting
widgets.title: Underfitting, overfitting, and the sweet spot
widgets.hint: Slide the flexibility (polynomial degree) · resample the data · watch the test error
widgets.pitch: More flexible models always fit the training data better, but past a point they predict new data worse.
widgets.data_doc: {x: number[], y: number[], xlabel?, ylabel?} (split into train/test inside)

widgets.name: cv_folds
widgets.title: K-fold cross-validation (and leakage)
widgets.hint: Press play to rotate the folds · switch the splitting scheme · compare with the truth line
widgets.pitch: Every sample gets a turn in the test set. Split by group (household, patient, bird) or shared group quirks leak across folds.

widgets.name: resampling
widgets.title: Bootstrap and permutation, built live
widgets.hint: Press play to resample · switch between bootstrap and permutation · watch the histogram grow
widgets.pitch: Resample your own data thousands of times to estimate sampling uncertainty (bootstrap) or test against a null hypothesis (permutation).
widgets.data_doc: {a: number[], b: number[], names?: [string, string], unit?: string}
